messages.text:
The only way I can think of is time-based "attack".
You may try to pass different passwords, sha256 hases of which start with different characters, and if you perform enough attempts and measure time accurately, then you may try to find statistical deviations for passwords, hashes of which do start with 1 known pattern and some other pattern.
---
But to perform this on practice, taking into account all the netwotrk biased fluctuations - it's almost impossible.
Also, there is no guarantee, that it compares sha256 hash and not some other, or that time-based attack guard is not implemented.

messages.text:
Ok, thank you for clarification.
Tested it myself, that both exercises are correct:
1. You can manually set K + IV to re-encode just decoded file and it would match original one.
2. You can do it with either correct password or with  wrong one. No difference. In both cases you will end up with "passed" check.
---
So, to conclude, there is actually no way to programmatically check if your password or resulting "bytes" are correct or not. Only heuristic assumptions may be to help, but it's almost certainly "all characters are printable" heuristic.

messages.text:
The anchor effect. An amazing feature of the psyche that allows knowledgeable people to manipulate and have power. Comparison and analogy play a crucial role here: if you give a person an anchor (a cognitive model for comparison), then he will tie the next object to it (compare it, take it as a model). There are plenty of examples. Take, for example, supermarkets with crossed—out price tags: if you see that this product used to cost $ 50, but now it costs $35, your mind will instantly appreciate the "profitability" of the offer, without thinking about the fact that the real price is $ 20 (or it costs nothing at all, you just don't need it). Or if you put a mattress on an expensive premium bed, to put it mildly, of average quality with an obviously overpriced price, it will fly away complete with furniture, without causing doubt to the buyer.


Lots of letters. I decide to stay with my "bullshit," but I know exactly where I'm going. Do you know? Of course, you "know". A person will kill himself to prove the correctness of his actions, even if this is not the case. I've been talking a lot these days, but I just want to help 😜

messages.text: You're right. I can only speak in such hints, as other hints will be too specific and then any decision will be worthless if I help someone. There are indeed more than one solutions and possible solutions. Rough work with Sulph and trying to disassemble it without knowing or understanding exactly what's going on in this puzzle is one of the worst ways (the lack of a solution in the last 4 years confirms this, and it's not about the complexity of this phase). The puzzle is really complicated, but that's because of its specificity. There is more psychology involved here and working with a person, his perception, than the need to have strong knowledge in programming or cryptography. This knowledge is extremely limited here (fortunately for me, not for example), but there is nowhere without it. However, it all comes down to what, where, why, and why. Attack any one small detail and the tangle will begin to unwind. It doesn't matter why I know something or why I'm trying to tell you. However, this is true. p.s. - different people just tried to write to me, and even offered some money, but it's not interesting at all. I'll just say what I can say for everyone to see. And if someone thinks about something and eventually understands me, I will be glad. In any case, everyone has the right to choose their own ways and approaches to solving problems.

I haven't done any puzzles for more than 4 years, in principle, it used to be fun for me and I, the guys, were making some progress with me. But of course as entertainment. I saw this puzzle a long time ago, we didn't even get any further than usual and completely forgot about it. And then, quite by chance, 1.5 months ago, I saw him again and decided to work. At first, I worked like everyone else does, but ordinary logic dictated that if so many people couldn't solve it in ANY WAY for so long, then do only what no one else did. I am glad that I was able to find something, there is some satisfaction, I have amused my ego. But the hole is deep and shallow at the same time.

It can be solved, easily and difficult (stupid, but so). Remember that a puzzle (even a cryptographic one) is a puzzle where logical judgment is closely intertwined with encryption. Try more simple ciphers. And just enjoy it without thinking about the prize. The road will be mastered by the walking.

messages.text: I'm not going to be a bully with longnids anymore. There are many things in my messages that will help. You can believe it or not. I haven't solved the only two problems that I see in front of me at least. If you correctly interpret the hints of monsieur, who sometimes talks to you, you will decide. It's the same with my "bullshit." So, as the leader of the revolution, I allowed myself to draw some conclusions, although I am not smarter or better than others, that's for sure. And in any case, everyone still has time to make a decision. The puzzle game on my part is over, with some exceptions. I want to thank its creators. It's a beautiful and interesting thing. Generally, something that makes some good sense is always a good thing. The prize is also great, considering the cost of bitcoin. But personally, this path reminded me of what I always went for and how I did it (professionally). Think outside the box, this is what gives the price of life. That's where the money comes from, although it's the least you can get by living this way. I wish you all good luck and make it beautiful, as you created this puzzle. This is one of the rare things that occur in life, like really good books, like films with meaning, or like music, painting, or any art with meaning. Technology is great, we need it. But we must not forget that we are human beings and live by completely different laws. If the machines understand them, we risk falling into the matrix...

messages.text:
I'm trying to understand, I'm still analyzing until some clues make sense.

1.Meaning of "Archi"
Derived from the Greek ἀρχι- (arkhi-), meaning "origin," "government," or "command."

In The Matrix, the Architect is the creator and controller of the system.

It could relate to words like "archetype," "archenemy," or even "anarchy" (rejection of control).



2. "Matrixsumlist is not about numbers"

If it’s not mathematical, it could be a wordplay:

"Matrix" + "sum" (addition) + "list" → Could sound like "subliminal" (something hidden within the system).

Or it could mean "listing the essence of the Matrix," suggesting the search for a fundamental concept.


3. "Last words before first choice"

In the red pill/blue pill scene, Morpheus says:
"You take the blue pill... the story ends. You take the red pill... you stay in Wonderland."

The last word before the choice is "Wonderland," a direct reference to Alice in Wonderland.


4. "Salph" and "Anstoo"
"Salph" could be an anagram or word fusion:

"Sal" (jump in Spanish) + "ph" (pH scale, balance in chemistry).

Or "S Alpha," suggesting a beginning (Greek letter α).

"Anstoo" might sound like "answer two" or refer to "anstoss" (impulse, a concept in Fichte's philosophy).



5. Reference to Yin-Yang

Indicates duality: control and freedom, reality and illusion, system and rebellion.

The answer might be related to balance, transition, or opposition.


Possible Answers

1. "Archi" + "tect" = "Architect"

Since this answer was rejected by the group, it might need to be deconstructed.

"Archi" (origin) + "text" (code) → "Archi-text", meaning the foundation of the system.


2. "Anstoo" = "Answer Two"

If the answer is dual, it could involve words like "Simulation and Reality" or "Control and Freedom."


3. "Salph" = "Jump pH" → "Dimension Shift"

Might indicate a transition between realities, like Neo leaving the Matrix.

Possible answer: "Portal" or "Change."


4. "Wonderland" as the final clue

Neo follows the "rabbit hole," so the answer might be "Alice" or "Curiosity."




Most Likely Answer

The best guess is ARCHETYPE, because:

"Archi-" means origin, and "-type" means model.

In The Matrix, the Architect represents the archetype of control, while Neo is the archetype of rebellion.

It connects to the idea of recurring patterns within the simulation.


A Simpler Alternative

If it's something more direct, the answer could be "BEGIN," since the Architect emphasizes that "everything starts with a choice."

Update on this

Matrixsumlist- in the series it's often explained that "the one" is chosen to be the bearer of the sum of the errors in the matrix. We know that Neo is the 6th iteration of this, so we likely just need to list the iteration. This could also be the name of the iterations of the matrices themselves (the first matrix was the paradise matrix, while the second iteration was the nightmare iteration. Its important to note that only the first iteration is confirmed in the series and the other iterations are fan theories) 

Yinyang- the character sati in the series is one of the many forms of Shakti, and is the wife of Shiva who is the god of creation, perseverance and destruction. In Hinduism Shakti is considered as the primordial cosmic energy and represents the dynamic forces that are thought to move through the entire universe. This likely means that yinyang is sati, Shakti, or Shiva (or a combination of these)

Thepassword- this is more than likely a callback to the keymaker. The keymaker is a program. He carries an assortment of door keys that represent complex encryption passwords that can enter doors located in secret backdoor within the matrix.

messages.text: Consider two keyapirs, pubkey A with privkey a and pubkey B with privkey b. If you add the pubkeys together to get pubkey C, (A + B = C), C's private key c is also the sum of the two private keys, i.e. a + b = c. Furthermore, Schnorr signatures over the same message can be added together to produce a valid signature for the sum of the pubkeys, i.e. sig(a, msg) + sig(b, msg) = sig(c, msg)

I'm trying to think backwards. How was the DBBI code made? The prime numbers must have been inserted just to scramble the code because there's no cipher that would generate a code like this. So we need to eliminate these prime characters to try to decode what remains.

And what about FAED? Is it a continuation of DBBI? Does it follow the same rules? Should it be combined with DBBI in order to be decoded?

Let's think about how the codes might have been created and then work to undo them to see what remains.

text.text: Generate a vanity address for a third party using split-key

text:
It is possible to generate a vanity address for a third party in a safe manner using split-key.
For instance, Alice wants a nice prefix but does not have CPU power. Bob has the requested CPU power but cannot know the private key of Alice, Alice has to use a split-key.

Alice generates a key pair on her computer then send the generated public key and the wanted prefix to Bob. It can be done by email, nothing is secret. Nevertheless, Alice has to keep safely the private key and not expose it.
Note: The key pair is a standard SecpK1 key pair and can be generated with a third party software.
Bob runs VanitySearch using the Alice's public key and the wanted prefix.
It generates a keyinfo.txt file containing the partial private key.
Bob sends back this file to Alice. It can also be done by email. The partial private key does not allow anyone to guess the final Alice's private key.
Alice can then reconstructs the final private key using her private key (the one generated in step 1) and the keyinfo.txt from Bob.

text.text: VanitySearch.exe -rp L4U2Ca2wyo721n7j9nXM9oUWLzCj19nKtLeJuTXZP3AohW9wVgrH keyinfo.txt Pub Addr: 1ALicegohz9YgrLLa4ADCmam7X2Zr6xJZx Priv (WIF): p2pkh:L1NHFgT826hYNpNN2qd85S7F7cyZTEJ4QQeEinsCFzknt3nj9gqg Priv (HEX): 0x7BC226A19A1E9770D3B0584FF2CF89E5D43F0DC19076A7DE1943F284DA3FB2D0

Want a different theory that is new to this chat??? 

It's simple, I'll share it.... 

Not saying in any way that it's right either, just trying to get fresh eyes on different angles I'm working with this thing....

"Rabbit grid" and "seedisplanted"

- If we have a phase 2 and 3 that are clearly labeled with these numbers, then what exactly is phase 1???
- Does this imply that the rabbit is phase 0???

Theory - 
  
What if:

    "rabbit grid" = half 

and 

    "seedisplanted" = "better half"

( 2 halves of a single phase )

Reasoning:
    
    All phases in puzzle have followed a similar format; self contained and small enough even to fit 2 phases on a single page... 

Examples being 2 & 3, also Salph & Cosmic

    From here, it's all speculation, but trying to be realistic and keep things simple.... 

1. Rabbit grid contained binary URL
    - Also hashing text led to URL endpoint
    - So what's left to find??? Idk maybe nothing, but yellow blue primes hint strongly points back to the grid again
    - And this may be nothing as well, but the puzzle obviously was made by and belongs to GSMG, but why is their "G" logo on the puzzle image??? 
(Honestly, everything on the image has to do with the puzzle but the "G", kinda out of place, right?)

2. Seedisplanted images were not fully used...
    - the colors have what meanings???
    - the black "bank" is only known as such because of its filename, but what is purpose or meaning of the "bank"???
    - the unused word "crypto" from the images
    - etc. I'll save you guys from my extra long posts on this one....

3. The fact that only the rabbit grid and seedisplanted pages are image based, while all else in the puzzle is text...
    - Clear connection here
    - colors used went from :
    2 whites
    1 black
    1 blue
    1 yellow
    1 red (bottom border of grid)
    6 total colors for rabbit grid

    Reduced to:
    1 white
    1 black
    1 red
    1 blue
    4 total for seedisplanted


Only pointing out what they share and differ on but also the fact they were unused details...

Yellow and blue originally just pointed out the binary by spacing them every 8 squares (but the colors had a purpose)

The colors of seedisplanted are most likely used for same reason but obviously not for encoding binary...

- Side theory -
   
    Since Salph was reached by hashing the text of rabbit grid and Jrk showing disbelief that nobody has found the third door yet, it's a believable possibility that hashing text of seedisplanted (all or parts, idk) could lead to this third door as well.... I only say that because the entire puzzle has been consistent in its setup, ie: 

Phases 2 & 3
Same page setup and "solve the aes blob to move on" style as
Salph & Cosmic

So if hashing text of first image based puzzle phase goes somewhere, than why not the other image based phase piece as well???

I'll end here... Hope it helps someone....
Good luck everybody

messages.text:
Bitcoin mining is very often described as solving a "puzzle"

When miners solve the puzzle they are allowed to spend the block reward which is halved every 210.000 blocks. These transactions are called coinbase transactions.

The miners simply hash the transactions they want to include in their block, (the seed) until they find a hash that matches the difficulty prefix which is a digest that has the required leading 0s.

The coinbase transaction (spending the reward) is the first transaction in the block. the miner then have to wait 100 more blocks before they can spend the bitcoins

That's why I don't pretend.

Most likely, that it's obsllete bug of some online QR code generator. It's not necessarily result of JPEG compression. It could be result of some transforms, like scaling predefined finder pattern to given size.
E.g.

has feature to select one of predefined "eyes" shape and specify output image dimentions.

My point is that there is no much information "hidden" in those patterns and most likely they are artifacts of whatever operation, but not manually added by authors.

Best regards.

text:
The Silence of the Jrk.
for

, and free thinkers

Jrk wrote a path in layered code—
A quiet start, then a rising load.
Phase zero came without a fight,
Too smooth, too fast, it felt too light.

We marked it done and moved ahead,
Chasing echoes thet deeper led.
Phase one curved sharp, phase two burned slow,
Each step a fiction dressed as flow.

Then came the branching: phase three broke—
Into fragments, smoke on smoke.
Three point one spun webs with care,

messages.text:
Here a tutorial to use Mara Slipstream and avoid bots stealing your bitcoin

1. Choose the wallet you want to transfer to.

2. Hit Max button to transfer all the amount available.

3. Hit Pay button.

4. See the minimum fee Mara needs to mine your transaction (it’s not the same all the time).

5. Choose a fee slightly above the minimum fee of Mara (If minimum at current time is 20, choose 50 so you have your transaction included and prioritized at the next block).

6. Hit Preview button (DONT EVER PRESS “OK” BUTTON).

7. Sign your transaction with sign button (BE CAREFUL TO NOT HIT "BROADCAST” BUTTON BY MISTAKE).

8. Go to share button and export your transaction with Save to file and save the file wherever you want.

9. Close the preview window to avoid making a mistake you'll regret forever.

10. Open your file in notes and copy the Hex transaction.

11. Paste it in slipstream Mara and activate your transaction.

I used a standard Base64-to-raw-data conversion process.

42f5f4b7cbf78cf078a24a6ca7179b462eac13504c9791c8f1192ef8a7a352a4ef756397ea74234a97a95f01ae37f8c9

text:
When I think of "dbbib..." and "INCASEYOUMANAGETOCRACKTHIS..." it reminds me of a finding that I made back in April, which I mentioned again a couple of months ago. 

Not gonna bore you guys with the details, but everything is outlined in this message:

Basically I suggested that "dbbib..." might have been encrypted using a one-time pad with "INCASEYOUMANAGETOCRACKTHIS..." serving as the encryption key. The decrypted output contains the phrase "YOUWON".  I believe this might be the most progress anyone has made in deciphering even a small portion of legible text from "dbbib". 

I'm unsure what the other portions of the output could represent but I might have an idea. I observed that the number of characters which come after "YOUWON" is 64, which corresponds to the exact number of hexadecimal characters required to construct a Bitcoin private key. messages.text:
For the "Cosmic Duality" Block (the big Base64 block):

Starts with U2FsdGVkX18...: This is the Base64 encoding of Salted__.

Implication of Salted__: This prefix is a standard signature of the encryption format used by the openssl enc utility.

By default, openssl enc uses AES (usually AES-256-CBC or AES-128-CBC).

It also derives the key and IV from the provided password and the salt (the 8 bytes following Salted__) using a method called EVP_BytesToKey (which by default uses MD5 for hashing).

Conclusion for "Cosmic Duality": This is extremely likely to be AES in the OpenSSL format.  The decryption failure (the "padding is incorrect" error you encountered) points much more to a bad password or, less likely, a different hashing algorithm used in key derivation (other than MD5 or SHA256 which we have already tested), than to a completely different cipher algorithm like Rabbit. If it were Rabbit, the Salted__ prefix would either not be there or would have a different meaning.

Here’s a Python script that I wrote to extract messages from a specific user in a Telegram group chat. This was used to compile the file that I shared in my previous message.

To use it, you should first export the group chat as JSON.

When running the script, you need to specify the path to the exported JSON file which contains all group messages. You also have to specify the name of the user whose messages you want to extract.

The results will then be printed to the console. To save the results, you can simply pipe the output to a .txt file.

Usage Example:
python3 get_messages_from_export.py /path/to/result.json --user "username" > messages.txt"

For any coders in here, please feel free to improve the script.

text_entities.text:
I made what I believe is a pretty big finding a few days ago when it comes to "dbbib..." and "faed...". 

Basically after using various ciphers I found that a small portion of "faed..."  can be decoded via Bifid cipher using a period of 570, with some of the first characters of "dbbib..." serving as the alphabet keyword.

messages.text:
Bifid Alphabet Keyword: 
"dbbibfbhccbegbihabebeihbeggegebebbgehhebhhfbabfdhbeffcdbbfcccgbfbeeggecbedcibfbffgigbeeeabe"

You could use the entirety of "dbbib" for this...

Or You can just extract first 13 characters, remove the duplicates and you'll get: "dbifhceg"
This is really all one needs for the alphabet keyword, and should be the correct way of doing it.

Generated Bifid Key (J Removed): "DBIFHCEGAKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"

Bifid Ciphertext (All the characters of "faed"): 
"faedggeed..."

Bifid Period: 570 (Length of ciphertext)

Result:
""

A potential find in first seven characters. Can't make this shit up!!:
"btcseed"

And then you have the rest to be solved:
"deoemckeadhbschdkb..."

I have not gotten much farther then this.

With this I did not find anything substantial. However, when I take the Trifid decode and XOR it with a hex key of "26", the resulting text will start with the word: "chao". 

This is the Spanish translation of the Italian word "ciao", meaning both "hello" and "goodbye".  In the context of the puzzle, the definition of the word implies the concept of "yinyang".

Could this allude to the use of the word found in Phase 3.2 and various hints? Or maybe even a hint to use a Chaocipher? Could just be a coincidence and entirely unrelated. Not to sure at this point tbh since we're pretty deep in the rabbit hole.

import itertools as it, re, base64, base58, binascii, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

# --- helpers ------------------------------------------------------------
PAL={'B':(0,0,0),'W':(255,255,255),'L':(63,72,204),'Y':(255,242,0)}
def lab(v): return min(PAL,key=lambda k:np.linalg.norm(v-PAL[k]))
def read(p,bw=False):
    img=np.array(

(p).convert('RGB')); s=img.shape[0]//33
    m=np.empty((33,33),'U1')
    for r,c in it.product(range(33),repeat=2):
        y,x=r*s+s//2,c*s+s//2
        col=lab(img[y,x])
        m[r,c]='B' if bw and col=='B' else col
    if bw:m[m!='B']='W'
    return m
def flips(bw,col):
    for r,c in it.product(range(33),repeat=2):
        if col[r,c] in('L','Y') and bw[r,c]!=col[r,c]:
            yield r,c

# --- version-4 function mask + order ------------------------------------
F=np.zeros((33,33),bool)
def finder(r0,c0):
    F[r0:r0+7,c0:c0+7]=True

    for r in rows:
        for dx in(0,1):
            x=col-dx
            if not F[r,x]: ORDER.append((r,x))
    up=not up; col-=2

def main(qr1,qr2):
    bw,col=read(qr1,True),read(qr2)
    M=np.array(bw=='B',bool)
    for r,c in flips(bw,col): M[r,c]=not M[r,c]
    bits=''.join('1' if M[r,c] else '0' for r,c in ORDER)
    payload_bytes=bytes(int(bits[i:i+8],2) for i in range(0,528,8))
    print(f"\nRaw bytes (66): {payload_bytes.hex()}")
    try: print("ASCII:",payload_bytes.decode('ascii'))
    except: pass
    b58=base58.b58encode(payload_bytes).decode()

    bech32chars='023456789acdefghjklmnpqrstuvwxyz'

messages.text:
Phase 3.2 is based on The Matrix: Reloaded movie which in turn is deeply based on the Alice Through the Looking Glass novel. 

The way I came to the conclusion that the novel has something to do with the phase is from this line:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A fubcd-king & oracle-queen, thingky mvps, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

Remove the characters that were used in the alphabet to solve the Vic cipher and your left with this:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A -king & -queen, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

This entire text I interpret as having to do with a game of chess and not a straddling checkerboard as some have suggested. What is Alice Through the Looking Glass based on? A literal game of chess. 

The first page of the novel includes an actual chess board ("first one seen"), the chess board includes a black king (-king) and a black queen (-queen). What is the opposite/negative of white? It's black. A chess board usually has white and black squares. This all ties into the concept of yin yang.

How many pieces dose one player get in a game of chess? It is 16 which may allude to the "sixteen encryptions" that are mentioned in Phase 3.2. The chess board in the novel also has 8 pieces. With the pawn represented as Alice. When you exclude Alice your left with 7 chess pieces, which might have to do with the "seven intertwined passwords" mentioned. Alice also dose seven moves in order to get promoted to Queen.

Of course this is all conjecture, so take my interpretation with a grain of salt.

messages.text:
making a case for steganography:

    1. Steg (shorthand use for this post)
        - Phase 0 rabbit image contains a binary spiral with every 8 bits ending with a blue or yellow square
          This is obfuscation instead of encryption which is Steg 100%

    2. Phase 1 seedisplanted
        -  Images here with words are simply scrambled to once again obfuscate what we are looking for

    3. Phase 3 (Decentraland Hint)
        -  Mp3 file obtained here with 100% Steg used to hide the message "HASHTHETEXT"
           No encryption used here, only obfuscation

    4. Unused piece of Phase 0 rabbit image
        -  The infamous FEFE square
           Only visible on Bit plane 0 of all RGB layers
           Bit plane 0 is most known for LSB Steg

    5. Key argument here that has been misunderstood by many, when making arguments for Steg being used to hide what we are looking for; within the rabbit image...

    -  Just so we are all looking at this from the correct perspective, I challenge anyone to find a program (or create one even), that is capable of finding the binary spiral and decoding it, that was not specifically made to do just that (because it seems like only Steg searching software has been used so far on this)... The point is, no software existed that could do this before the puzzle was made (this is why no Steg has yet been found)… Steg is not always something that takes a CTF challenge method to solve (Binary spiral and seedisplanted image shuffling are proof of this)… 

    6. So I am asking anyone that is willing to take another look at the rabbit grid again (without relying only on Steg tools), to see if there really might be something else here (there obviously is —>FEFE)… Hopefully we can get something new to work with even if we don't know how to use whats found after we find it... Just a thought

< ON NIHILISM > 
Nihilism no longer wears the dark, Wagnerian, Spenglerian, fuliginous colors of the end of
the century. It no longer comes from a Weltanschauung of decadence nor from a
metaphysical radicality born of the death of God and of all the consequences that must be
taken from this death. Today's nihilism is one of transparency, and it is in some sense
more radical, more crucial than in its prior and historical forms, because this transparency,
this irresolution is indissolubly that of the system, and that of all the theory that still
pretends to analyze it. When God died, there was still Nietzsche to say so - the great
nihilist before the Eternal and the cadaver of the Eternal. But before the simulated
transparency of all things, before the simulacrum of the materialist or idealist realization
of the world in hyperreality (God is not dead, he has become hyper-real), there is no
longer a theoretical or critical God to recognize his own.

messages.text:
If I split the string "dbbi" into 7 parts (the size of matrixsumlist), and use the first part as a key in faed, we get something like "btcseed...". Taking that result (the full "btcseed" string) and using it with the next part of "dbbi", we get something like "can...", and so on for the remaining parts, we get:

dbbibfbhccbeg -> "btcseed..."
bihabebeihbeg -> "bar..."
gegebebbgehhe -> ""
bhhfbabfdhbef -> "can..."
fcdbbfcccgbfb -> "fee..."
eeggecbedcibf -> ""
bffgigbeeeabe -> ""
```
It’s probably just a coincidence, but all of them appear at the beginning of the text and are BIP39-valid
```

messages.text:
The unbalanced matrix grid thats 75x75 pixels 13x13 blocks and most right block beeing 73x75, while the bottom row beeing 75x73 imo is just a red herring. A carefully constructed anomaly that protects the prize =).

The reason i spent so much time focusing on the puzzle image itself was grounded in the fact that Jrk is a OG bitcoiner, and they are all from that era where paper wallets were the standard for security. Paper wallets always have the address printed on it together with a QR code like this puzzle image. These guys like Jrk are obsessed with security and it's a very common thing that they say that you should print the wallet, never let it touch the internet etc, so it makes sense that the rest of the puzzle was in reality just a showcasing how to protect a private key by making the masses believe there is a puzzle, when in reality, the privkey was hidden in the main puzzle itself since the beginning. It's a genious idea to be honest, and since Jrk already fooled us with the april 1st puzzle, it would be a cool plot twist. I've even spent hundreds of hours looking for the private key in the april 1st puzzle.

Even though it may take a 1000 hours to accept it, finally we have to accept that the puzzle really is a puzzle/challenge with real steps and phases

def tBacon(s:str) -> str:
    return ''.join( bin(~i & 0b11111)[2:].zfill(5).translate(str.maketrans('01','ba')) for i in [ ord(s[j]) ^ 0x7f for j in range(len(s)) ] )

def fBacon(s:str) -> str:
    return ''.join( chr(~int(s[i:i+5].translate(str.maketrans('ab','01')),2) & 0b1111111) for i in range(0,len(s),5))

messages.text:
AES-256-CBC doesn't have "infinite" valid outputs. With the Salted__ format and standard KDF, a correct password produces a single artifact. Wrong passwords result in "bad decryption" or noise (and the fact that two different keys give EXACTLY the same binary is negligible).

Correct decryption is stable and verifiable by hash: SHA-256 of the artifact = 4f7a1e4efe4bf6c5581e32505c019657cb7b030e90232d33f011aca6a5e9c081. If someone obtains something else, they are not using the same key or the same pipeline.

This artifact is designed not to be readable text. It is used as an intermediate structure with consistent cryptographic outputs; there is no "plain message" hidden there.

The next step is not inside the binary. It requires "HASHTHETEXT" from an external text from the author (cases/exact spaces). Without that text, progress cannot be made toward the prize address.

If anyone claims otherwise, please share reproducible evidence: the same SHA-256 and a procedure that derives the prize address. Without that, it's speculation.

messages.text:
They're displaying the base64-decoded or garbage blob, not the plaintext. "Salted__ + salt + ciphertext" will always be identical for any password; that explains "first 64 bytes are the same." What matters is the plaintext after AES, not the base64 result.
In AES-256-CBC, two different passwords with the same 64-byte plaintext prefix have a probability of ~2^-512. Practically impossible.

messages.text:
ME → drop the stray “ME”

WISEMAN → use the “wise man” hint (it points to the heart target line)

U → remove the extra U in misspellings (e.g., FOURTY → FORTY)

I → remove the extra I (WAISTING → WASTING)

C → change C to Z (PRICES → PRIZES)

H → drop the extra H (THROPHIES → TROPHIES)

THE → remove the extra “THE” (e.g., “FUNCTION OF THE YOU”)

S → drop the odd plural S (“SOURCE CODES” → “SOURCE CODE”)

ANDOR → treat “AND OR” as the instruction choose one (use OR)

NOTE → remove NOTE (“KEYNOTE” → “KEY”)

NESS → remove “NESS” (“ENTIRENESS” → “ENTIRE”)

SELF → remove the duplicate SELF (“YOURSELF SELF” → “YOURSELF”)

O → drop the dangling O (“CIAO BELLA O” → “CIAO BELLA”)

All the block ciphers normally use PKCS#5 padding, also known as standard block padding. This allows a rudimentary integrity or password check to be performed. However, since the chance of random data passing the test is better than 1 in 256 it isn't a very good test.

If padding is disabled then the input data must be a multiple of the cipher block length.( inverse is the same )

text: If you look at

, you can also make a pretty good use for the unused things there.

The «S» in the black box and «crypto» and «lock» and «lO» can be ysed again:

Scrypt IO lock,

Which is exactly what bip38 uses. Scrypt which is bound by I/O - making it extremely slow to bruteforce compared to something like pbkdf2

——

There are 2 ways you can use BIP38. The first is to encrypt an existing private key with a password.

The second way to use BIP38 is to let someone else create a private key for you and not allow them to spend your Bitcoins.  So if you buy a physical Bitcoin for example, you’ll notice they have a private key printed on them and the guy who created them knows that key. So having BIP38 allows the creation of these coins and still protect you from the seller’s ability to spend them.

Bip38 is widely used in vanity generation services and encrypting of paper wallets

messages.text:
Phase 3.2 is based on The Matrix: Reloaded movie which in turn is deeply based on the Alice Through the Looking Glass novel. 

The way I came to the conclusion that the novel has something to do with the phase is from this line:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A fubcd-king & oracle-queen, thingky mvps, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

Remove the characters that were used in the alphabet to solve the Vic cipher and your left with this:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A -king & -queen, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

This entire text I interpret as having to do with a game of chess and not a straddling checkerboard as some have suggested. What is Alice Through the Looking Glass based on? A literal game of chess. 

The first page of the novel includes an actual chess board ("first one seen"), the chess board includes a black king (-king) and a black queen (-queen). What is the opposite/negative of white? It's black. A chess board usually has white and black squares. This all ties into the concept of yin yang.

How many pieces dose one player get in a game of chess? It is 16 which may allude to the "sixteen encryptions" that are mentioned in Phase 3.2. The chess board in the novel also has 8 pieces. With the pawn represented as Alice. When you exclude Alice your left with 7 chess pieces, which might have to do with the "seven intertwined passwords" mentioned. Alice also dose seven moves in order to get promoted to Queen.

Of course this is all conjecture, so take my interpretation with a grain of salt.

messages.text:
It's not flawed. That change applies to the OpenSSL CLI "default"; the Salted__ blob doesn't record which digest was used. You have to derive with the SAME digest used when encrypting.

Here, MD5 in EVP_BytesToKey is what works: it decrypts with valid padding, returns the expected unpadded SHA-256, and allows re-encryption by reproducing the exact ciphertext.

If it had been SHA-256, MD5 would fail. You can parameterize the KDF (MD5/SHA-256) to check this, but practical evidence points to MD5.

messages.text:
Is it just me, or does it feel like the puzzle intentionally steered us onto a path that might never have been solvable?

Take the SalPhaseIon / Cosmic Duality segment. It’s completely standalone — something that could have been added or activated at any time without disturbing the earlier stages.

Back in 2019, when the puzzle first launched, it only took a few weeks for solvers to push all the way into Phase 3.3, which was thought to be the endgame. At that point, the creator suddenly announced:

“Dear all, somebody pointed out that there might be a mistake in phase III and that is correct unfortunately. The mistake makes it nearly impossible to solve unless you'd know where to add 1 extra character between the 3 answers. My sincerest apologies for this, I'll fix this as soon as I've found a decent spot to do so… Again, 1000 times sorry, I'm aware I might have wasted a lot of time for some :-(…” (2019-05-17)

Shortly after, they gave the “fix”:

“Here’s the hint in order to bypass the mistake:
giveit = givetit” (2019-05-17)

The strange thing is that some groups had already managed to decrypt the section without ever needing that correction. Still, the creator insisted on applying it. What exactly was changed behind the scenes, only the creator knows.

But here’s the most telling part: just a day later, they openly admitted their shock at how fast people had advanced:

“So, after yesterday's 'hint' a team of puzzlers has made an unbelievable amount of progress in just one day… The progress they made was unforeseen as we expected it to take at least a !month! to pass those parts of the puzzle. Hat off for those that managed… we stand in awe for you.” (2019-05-18)

And then, almost immediately, they dangled something new:

“In case the private key hasn't been found in 2019 we'll release a tiny hint at the start of 2020, that will be the final hint. Can the private key be retrieved without that hint? Yes.” (2019-05-18)

So within the span of a few minutes — first expressing genuine surprise that Phase 3.3 had been solved much faster than expected, and then offering hints for a “new phase” — the puzzle itself branched.

That’s why it feels like the path we’re on now was never the intended conclusion, but rather an extension designed to prolong engagement once the original design was cracked too quickly.

Just to be clear — this is only speculation, not accusation.
It’s been six years without a full solve, and it makes me wonder if maybe the puzzle was extended or branched after Phase 3 was solved so quickly. That wouldn’t be a bad thing — it would make sense to keep engagement alive.

I’m not pointing fingers at anyone, just sharing a thought. And if even raising this idea gets me removed, then that kind of proves the point. At the end of the day, we’re all here for the same reason: to enjoy and eventually solve this puzzle.

I think there's a hint there

Since all blocks are 75x75 except the bottom row and right column, it's sort of like an alignment pattern, and it creates 26 anamolies. the bottom rows most right beeing the only one 72x72 a hint towards QR codes, since they are read starting from the bttom most right..

each rabbit's block is the same amount of pixels thats missing from each of the 26 anamoly blocks in the alignment pattern, which also means that each 75x75 block can be divided by 25, so 25x25 is the correct QR code to use for the privkey.

the whole puzzle image is way to "paper-wallet" styled. it has everything, except the qr code for the privkey =) probably has both the QR code custom encoded there in the matrix grid, and the seed somewhere below the matrix in another custom way. probably need to retrieve some key or something from the phases and use. i will try all glhf

messages.text:
Similarities in the Concept of Cosmic Duality between Archie Comics and The Matrix

Choice as the Center of Cosmic Duality

In both stories, the main characters (Archie and Neo) face choices that reflect a cosmic duality—Betty vs. Veronica, the Matrix vs. the real world. Neither fully resolves these choices before their "death," creating a perpetual cosmic tension. Archie's last words and Trinity's declaration before Neo's resurrection are moments where this duality is highlighted without resolution.

Death as a Balancer for Duality

Archie's death in Life with Archie #36 and Neo's temporary death in The Matrix are culminating points that maintain the cosmic duality. Archie dies without choosing, maintaining the balance between Betty and Veronica. Neo dies but resurrects, maintaining the balance between the Matrix and the real world. Both are cosmic sacrifices to maintain the narrative.

Multiverse/Simulation as a Reflection of Duality

Archie Comics uses the multiverse (Betty vs. Veronica's timeline) to explore duality, just as The Matrix uses simulation vs. reality. In both cases, the main characters are trapped in a cycle that maintains this duality, with last words or critical moments symbolizing cosmic uncertainty.

Love as a Cosmic Force

Love is the element that transcends duality in both stories. Archie chooses not to choose because he loves both, maintaining balance. Neo rises because of Trinity's love, bridging the Matrix and the real world. This reflects the cosmic idea that love is an impartial, balancing force.

Archie Comics Series with Correlates to Cosmic Duality
All of the aforementioned series (Life with Archie, Archie Marries Veronica / Archie Marries Betty, Archie: The Decision, Afterlife with Archie, the main Archie series) have elements of cosmic duality, primarily through:

Love Triangle as Yin-Yang: Betty and Veronica are the two poles that maintain the balance of Riverdale.
Death and Resurrection: Archie frequently "dies" (literally or metaphorically) and comes back to life, resembling a cosmic cycle.
Multiverse: Alternate timelines reflect the duality of reality, similar to the Matrix simulation.

Specific Examples:

Life with Archie #36: Archie's death is the culmination of a cosmic duality, with his last words symbolizing the balance between Betty and Veronica.
Archie: The Decision (2024): The pressure to choose is a cosmic battle, but Archie remains ambiguous, maintaining the duality.
Afterlife with Archie: Zombie world vs. normal Riverdale is a cosmic duality, with Archie as the balance.

Conclusion
The concept of "last words before Archie's choice" and elements of The Matrix are connected to cosmic duality through the themes of ambiguous choice, death as a balance, and love as a cosmic force. In Archie Comics, Betty and Veronica are a yin-yang duality maintained through Archie's uncertainty. In The Matrix, Neo navigates the duality of the Matrix vs. the real world, with Trinity's love as a balance. Both use death and last words to maintain cosmic balance without a final resolution, reflecting the eternal cycle inherent in cosmic duality.

3. Uncertainty across time

At this second, you can measure: on or off.
At the next second, you don’t know yet — only the potential exists.
So binary isn’t just a static code, it’s a temporal dance: the certainty of “now” and the uncertainty of “next.”

This introduces entropy, probability, information. Claude Shannon essentially formalized this: information = reduction of uncertainty when a symbol arrives.

Convert image to raw scanlines.

Each line starts with a filter-byte, so we have 1556 filterbytes.

Filterbytes are between 0x00 to 0x04, so count how many of each filterbyte we have.

0x04 = 0
0x03 = 0
0x02 = 1464
0x01 = 91
0x00 = 1

Intresting..

91 filterbytes 0x01 
dbbi = 91 characters
incaseyoumanagetocrackthis... = 91 characters
91 bytes = 192 chars (

is 192 bits)


Next, we have only 1 filterbyte 0x00.

Very intresting and unusual.

Which line has the 0x00 filterbyte?
Remember when we are counting, do we start counting from 0 or 1? You choose.
counting_from_0 = line 1416
counting_from_1 = line 1417

How did we solve the Decentraland piece? Split 2 channels, reverse half..
What are the decentraland coordinates? [-41,-16 and -41,-17].

Split the line indexes in half, we get [14,16 and 14,17]. reverse half, we get 41,16 and 41,17.

Next, let's see how many lines are left after the 0x00 filterbyte line..
spoiler-alert: 140 lines

The 0x00 filterbyte appears in the QR code, so lets look at where in the QR code.. So start at the top of the QR code and count each line until we find the line with the 0x00 filterbyte. (again, count from 0 or 1?). So how many lines from the top of the qr code?

counting_from_0 = 127
counting_from_1 = 128

127 = max ascii value (128 since its counting from 0).


Let me know if anyone have any ideas!

text:
Thinking about the fact that dbbi has 91 character positions separated by space - its 181 length with the space.

counting from 1 and connecting B-E on yellow primes, the only place where yellow doesnt align with BE is on position 73. position 72 is where FEFEFE block is.

anyways, after connecting the entire pattern we end up with 83 positions instead of 91. This makes the string length 171 instead of 181. (171 when counting with a 0-index). the real length is 172.

Don't know if it makes sense, but 83 + 171 is also 254, which is 0xFE. if we use (1-indexing instead of 0-indexing, we get 83+172 = 255, which is max 8-bit value).

fefefe is at position 5,8 and one of base58 features is that it selects all characters when u double click it. If you doubleclick the 7-passwords string, we get 172 characters. So this 171/172 is also found in the whiteline pixels below the redline, which also happens to be 171 pixels wide.

All these things seems to be connected. Blocks in the 14x14 grid too, except the bottom row and right row, where they are 72px. remember fefefe is at position 72 in the prime pattern too.

And lastly, we have 24 blue/yellow blocks which is 8 bit bytes. Total 196 blocks, where the last 4 are ignored so far. If we remove the MSB for the entire 24 bytes (since its always 0 anyways) and treat it as 7-bit bytes instead of 8, we see the number again.. (192 - 24) = 168 + (4 last 0 bits) = 172 remaining bits.

Rabbit blocks is also defined by 37 blocks, which is 73 in reverse

There is some logic that we havent discovered, there's simply too many coincidences.

"

" to binary also has 91 0s.
The puzzle image raw scanlines has 91 filterbytes that are 0x01 and a single 0x00 filterbyte. the remaining 1464 of them are filterbyte  0x02.

text.text:
a computer program written in the esoteric visual programming language **Piet**. Although it looks like abstract pixel art with an animal at the center, its function is very specific: when executed by an interpreter (like the one you shared), this program **prints the text "Hello, world!"** on the screen.

The animal figure (usually seen as a donkey or rabbit) is not a command, but rather an artistic way of using "walls" (black blocks) and "empty spaces" (white blocks) to force the program to follow a precise path through the colored blocks, ensuring that the correct instructions are executed in the correct order.

---
### **Detailed Explanation**

Let's break down the components and how it works:

#### 1. What is the Piet Language?
Piet is a programming language where the source code is a graphic image (a bitmap) instead of text.  The flow of execution is guided by a "pointer" that moves from one colored region to another. The action to be performed is determined by the change in color and brightness between the block the pointer leaves and the block it enters.

#### 2. The Role of Elements in the Image

* Colored Blocks (Blue, Yellow, etc.):
* These are the program's "commands." Each contiguous colored block is called a "codel."
* The transition from a blue codel to a yellow codel, for example, corresponds to a specific instruction, such as "add two numbers on the stack" or "print a character."

* Black Blocks:
* These act as **walls**. The execution pointer cannot enter a black block.
* When the pointer encounters a wall, it is forced to change direction (usually trying to turn right). This is essential for creating mazes and controlling the program's flow.

 * **White Blocks:**
* These are **neutral spaces** or "bridges." The execution pointer "glides" over the white blocks without executing any instructions and without changing direction.
* They are used to connect different parts of the program without interfering with the logic.

* **The Animal Figure (Donkey/Rabbit):**
* This is the most ingenious and artistic part of the program. The figure is constructed entirely of **black and white blocks**.
* **Structural Function:** Because it is made of "walls" (black) and "empty spaces" (white), its sole function is to create a complex and mandatory path for the execution pointer. It forces the pointer to navigate around the figure, passing through the colored blocks in the exact sequence required to generate the ASCII codes for "H", "e", "l", "l", "o", ",", " ", "w", "o", "r", "l", "d", "!".

#### 3. Like "Hello, world!"  Generated

The program works by manipulating numbers in a data structure called a stack. Execution follows a logic similar to this:

1. Start: The program starts in the upper left corner.
2. Path: The pointer moves across the image, following the path allowed by the colors and blocked by the black walls.
3. Calculations: When moving from one color to another, it performs mathematical operations (such as push, add, multiply) to construct the numerical values corresponding to the ASCII codes of each letter. For example, to generate 'H', it calculates the number 72.
4. Printing: After calculating the value of a character, it executes the output(char) command, which pops the number from the stack and prints it as a character on the screen.
5. Repetition: The process repeats for each character in the sentence "Hello, world!".  6. **End:** At the end, the pointer reaches a color combination that executes the command to end the program.

In short, the image is a brilliant fusion of programming logic and visual art. It uses the rules of an unusual programming language to transform a maze of pixels into one of the most iconic phrases in computing.

* **The Animal Figure (Donkey/Rabbit):**
* This is the most ingenious and artistic part of the program. The figure is constructed entirely of **black and white blocks**.
* **Structural Function:** Because it is made of "walls" (black) and "empty spaces" (white), its sole function is to create a complex and mandatory path for the execution pointer. It forces the pointer to navigate around the figure, passing through the colored blocks in the exact sequence required to generate the ASCII codes for "H", "e", "l", "l", "o", ",", " ", "w", "o", "r", "l", "d", "!".

The program works by manipulating numbers in a data structure called a stack. Execution follows a logic similar to this:

1. Start: The program starts in the upper left corner.
2. Path: The pointer moves across the image, following the path allowed by the colors and blocked by the black walls.

4. Printing: After calculating the value of a character, it executes the output(char) command, which pops the number from the stack and prints it as a character on the screen.
5. Repetition: The process repeats for each character in the sentence "Hello, world!".  6. **End:** At the end, the pointer reaches a color combination that executes the command to end the program.

messages.text:
It's very easy to create a mini key (I mean a valid one). I tried different methods and found about 100 "quite logical" ones inside this puzzle.

For example, take a random string of zeros and ones 24 characters long. Imagine this in ASCII as text in binary format (as it was in rikroll, binary code in binary code). Then delete every last 8th bit. You will get 168 bits, which is 29 base58 characters.

 Finally, add the prefix "S" to these 29 characters. You have obtained a private mini Bitcoin key that passes the validation test.  

Using this logic of formation. And information from the puzzle, building logical chains, you can find thousands of valid mini-keys.

messages.text:
The right information isn’t in the right hands. You guys here are suffering from apophenia. Until the few people who found the hidden structures share the information they discovered, the puzzle will not be solved. Those who found it, unfortunately, still haven’t understood how to use it. But there are people in the group who, if they receive this information, could solve the puzzle. The question is whether those people can overcome themselves and share this information, knowing that they would be giving away the key to the solution, the key they themselves couldn’t use.

Epistemic selfishness, combined with the keeper-of-secrets syndrome, has prevented any real progress in this group since 2021. Meanwhile, the others remain trapped in a state of apophenia mixed with a main-character syndrome...

messages.text:
I’m not asking for anything, and I don’t mean anything specific.
This is a question for those who are solving the puzzle.
Let’s assume you’ve discovered something - something that no one else has found. Naturally, that puts you one step closer to winning the reward. After you’ve already imagined the car of your dreams and the house you’d buy, you realize that the piece you found doesn’t actually help you because you lack the necessary knowledge to use it. Still, you’re certain it’s part of the solution, or at least part of the path toward it.
What’s the right thing to do?
Should you keep this piece to yourself, hoping that one day you’ll find the answer? Or should you share it with everyone - sacrificing the time and effort you’ve spent, but giving others a fair chance?
There are people who’ve found pieces like this and are now facing exactly this dilemma. Some have been stuck in it for years, staying in the group, waiting for one more hint to help them interpret what they’ve found and claim the reward. But there will be no more hints - everything that’s needed is already here.
So I believe the puzzle is now in the hands of a few people who have to make a choice. And the longer time passes, the harder it will be to make that choice, because the feeling of wasted time won’t let them share what they’ve found and finally “set themselves free.”
Or perhaps they’ll hope that one day, someone else will stumble upon that same obscure piece of information and be able to interpret it correctly - though that’s extremely unlikely.
At this point, I believe everything depends on those few people who must decide. Once the playing field is even, the first person who truly understands will deservedly take the keys.
Or maybe another 16 years will pass until the puzzle simply loses its appeal to those chasing money. Or maybe even sooner - once people gain access to 500–2000 logical qubit quantum computers capable of cracking any address with a public key. When that happens, Bitcoin’s value will likely collapse, as panic leads to mass conversion into other crypto assets.
So, I think you still have about 10 years to solve it — and after that, everything will be in your hands.✌️

When the puzzle halved to 2.5 BTC, bitcoin halved to 6.25 BTC.

Approximately in 2132, bitcoin will half it's reward from 4 satoshis to 2, while the puzzle will half it from 1 to 0 sats.

So the puzzles last halving will be 2 cycles before bitcoin

text.text:
Letter & GPS location — 

This method eliminates the need for a number pair, heightening strength at the cost of complexity. In this case, a geographic landmark is chosen that relates to a plot built around the given seed phrases. The GPS coordinates of this landmark dictate the placement of the seed phrases among the body of text. To maintain relatively easy dispersal with slight variation, every digit read increases by ten, so 21.493021 translates to: 2, 11, 24, 39,43, 50, 62, 71. This removes the need for a number pair as the numbers are themselves embedded into the location of the central landmark of a story.

Example:

Such an asset to be represented by an experienced and mature lawyer particularly when you have a trial in front of the Supreme Court of the USA. Load your argument with logic and do not provide ways to escape. Symbol of cultural diversity should be used as often as possible in order to support the story. Our client clearly did not make that complex and improvised bomb himself. They were on their way to his friend's picnic by the river when he noticed a suspicious person pretending to do aerobic exercises. He immediately pointed it out to his friends. Their whereabouts aren't a mystery, during the attack they were ordering ginger tea with honey to bring to the picnic.

Hey guys

I'm going to preface this with I am not selling anything and have zero interest in that. I just want to see this puzzle possibly progress. 

I've been working on creating a brutefroce method that incorporates alot of advance methods such as simulated annealing to try to brutefroce the priv key for the 1GSMG address. Better than tools like bit crack, etc. 

Now the likelyhood of actually ever hitting the actual address are small.. I mean... Mathematically you're more likely to win the lottery, but I'm constantly refining it and planning to release it here fully open source (it runs off a single html file) and you can self host it and look through the code yourself. 

My goal eventually is to add an optional pool-brute force method that allows people to optionally choose wether or not they'd like to dedicate resources (pauseable) to  contribute to the brute force however it will always remain an optional choice (which can be verified by looking at the source code.) 

Please do not DM me about this. I'll be releasing it to you guys soon. I intend for it to be extremely user friendly and entirely self hostable / offline compatible.

A script is a sequence of instructions written in a scripting language, designed to be executed directly by an interpreter at runtime, without a separate compilation step into machine code.

Python is a language and not «software» in that sense.

If he really meant python, his words means abolutely nothing, because python can literally do anything - its your choice what it does.

More likely when he says «same software was used in every phase» he is warning that guy that hes going too far, too complicated and simply reminding him that the puzzle is bound by the functions of a specific software

The script is just a set of instructions and says nothing about a specific language like python. You can make the exact same script in python, bash, shell, js, perl, ruby, lua and 100 other languages..

when you do almost anything with crypto in python, js or any of these scripting languages, they all use OpenSSL internally unless you write your own implementations of aes, ecdsa etc

text.text:
1. SalPhaseIon 
The a–b sequence was interpreted as binary, producing a salt. 
The a–i sequence was mapped to prime numbers and arranged into a 15x51 matrix. 
Prime columns were summed modulo 256, producing the SUMLIST. 
Final SUMLIST: 
99 c0 9e c0 7a b2 ac 6b 8b a7 8e 9c 93 95 a0 
2. Cosmic Duality 
The Base64 block corresponds to an OpenSSL ciphertext. 
Multiple candidate passwords derived from clues were tested. 
None yielded readable plaintext, confirming the goal was not narrative decryption. 
3. Convergence 
The SUMLIST contains 15 bytes (120 bits). 
Converted to Base32, it yields: 
thaj5qd2wkwgxc5hr2ojhfna 
Decoding Base32 returns the exact same bytes, 
demonstrating idempotence. 
4. Final Result 
The minimal ASCII interpretation yields: 
zk 
5. Conclusion 
The puzzle converges to a stable, minimum-entropy state. 
'zk' stands for Zero Knowledge: the proof is complete without further disclosure.
